blocks.text: HOCl and OCl- are both effective disinfectants, but HOCl is more effective because of its neutral charge, which lets it penetrate the cell walls of micro-organisms easily. Essential cellular components such as proteins and lipids are oxidised by HOCl and OCl-, disrupting cell function and leading to cell death; they also oxidise and inactivate enzymes crucial for the survival and replication of bacteria, and nucleic acids (DNA and RNA) can be oxidised, preventing bacteria from replicating and from vital cellular functions.

blocks.caption: How the active species kill bacteria
rows: oxidised, cell function disrupted, cell dies

blocks.prompt: Why is HOCl a more effective disinfectant than OCl- for killing bacteria in water (Quick Check 13.6a)?
blocks.explanation: HOCl carries no charge, so it passes through the bacterial cell wall and membrane far more easily than the negatively charged OCl- ion, which is repelled by the cell surface; once inside, HOCl oxidises proteins, enzymes and nucleic acids and the cell dies.

items: HOCl (neutral) penetrates cell walls better than OCl-; both oxidise proteins, lipids, enzymes and nucleic acids, killing bacteria or stopping replication.
